edits.after: Hu himself said that what pushed him down this road was a chain of small accidents: a farewell poem, a scare on a lake. He distrusted theories that explain all of history by a single cause, and liked to joke that accidents often matter more than any one cause that claims to explain everything. He also said the name of the collection, Experiments, showed the influence of the experimentalism of the American philosopher John Dewey: every theory is only a hypothesis, to be proved or disproved by actual trial. The vernacular had already proved itself in novels, Yuan drama and folk songs; poetry was the part left, the part he proposed to test with an experiment.

edits.before: 作者推断：这段经历最有意思的地方，是胡适把一场谁也说服不了谁的争论，变成了一个可以检验的问题。“白话不能作诗”是一句绝对的话，只要写出像样的白话诗，就能动摇它；不写，再多书信也只是各说各话。他先给诗集取名《尝试集》，等于先替自己定下了要举证的任务；他还在信里先写好了失败的退路，承认结果可能证明自己错了，这让它更像一场真正的试验，而不是换个方式继续辩论。发表时他把调子放低，陈独秀随后把旗子举高。
edits.after: 作者推断：把诗当作待检验的假设，是胡适自己的说法；从他的做法里还能多看出两点。一是他还没写出几首白话诗，就先给诗集取好名字，等于先替自己定下要举证的任务；二是他在信里先写好了失败的退路，承认这块新地可能是不毛之地，这让它更像一场真正的试验，而不是换个方式继续辩论。发表时他把调子放低，陈独秀随后把旗子举高。

edits.before: The author's inference: what is most interesting here is that Hu turned an argument nobody could win into a question that could be tested. The claim that the spoken language cannot be poetry is absolute; good vernacular poems would shake it, while without poems, any number of letters would remain a standoff. By naming his collection Experiments in advance, he in effect set himself the task of supplying the proof. In his letters he also wrote down his retreat in case of failure, accepting that the result might prove him wrong — which made it a real experiment rather than the argument continued by other means. When he published, he lowered his voice, and Chen then raised the banner.
edits.after: The author's inference: treating poetry as a hypothesis to be tested was Hu's own framing; his conduct shows two things more. First, he named the collection before he had written more than a few vernacular poems, in effect setting himself the task of supplying the proof. Second, in his letters he wrote down his retreat in case of failure, granting that the new land might prove barren — which made it a real experiment rather than the argument continued by other means. When he published, he lowered his voice, and Chen then raised the banner.
